doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "I support appropriate policing and enforcement alongside prevention, better public-space design, late-night safety, civilian and health responses where appropriate, and serious action on homelessness, mental illness and addiction." No Public Order Team and no bylaw-hours position. The sentence is scored once, on row 7 (M26b).

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "That means market and non-market housing, non-profit housing, supportive and complex-care housing, family-sized rentals, affordable paths to ownership and protection of existing lower-cost rental homes." Types named; no unit target, no composition share, no tenure percentage.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: An authorized campaign site with three guiding principles, ten priority areas, a biography, volunteer/pledge forms and a financial-agent authorization. Written and current. No numerical targets, costs, implementation dates or measure-by-measure delivery plan. /posts/hello-world/ and /pages/about/ are still template stubs.

cells.quote: That means market and non-market housing, non-profit housing, supportive and complex-care housing, family-sized rentals, affordable paths to ownership and protection of existing lower-cost rental homes.
cells.why: Agrees with a mixed composition as a goal. No unit target, no 3-bedroom share, no below-market share, no tenure percentage, no zoning or approval instrument. Context, not scored separately: "Victoria needs much more housing, but the goal cannot simply be more units." The demolition sentence is scored once, on row 21.

cells.quote: Public land should create lasting public value, and new development should consider affordability and displacement alongside supply.
cells.why: Agrees with the public-land-value goal M6b is built on. No City land bank, no acquisition fund, no co-op financing. Community-wealth "co-operatives" are economic actors, not housing co-ops, and are not scored here.

cells.quote: I support appropriate policing and enforcement alongside prevention, better public-space design, late-night safety, civilian and health responses where appropriate, and serious action on homelessness, mental illness and addiction.
cells.why: Commits to civilian and health responses as part of the safety mix. Comparable to M26b (civilian crisis response so the wrong responder stops absorbing officer time), not the same: no CRCL, IMCRT or VCOT named, no dispatch criteria, no funding figure. One sentence, one measure: homelessness in this list is not a second mark. Context: "Homelessness is not synonymous with crime, and public safety policy should focus on harmful behaviour rather than someone’s housing status or background."

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: City Hall should be at the centre of a proud, ongoing Buy Local campaign that encourages residents, businesses and public institutions to support our local economy.
cells.why: Commits to a named local-economy campaign. Comparable to M71's downtown/business instrument set, not the same: no vacancy target, no Strategic Economic Plan, no "one mandate not a new office." Context, same block, not scored separately: "Victoria should be one of the best small cities in the world to start a business," and City Hall as a stronger partner on transportation, clean and safe streets, employee housing and infrastructure. Local-procurement wording in the same block is the same claim and is not scored again on row 47.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: City hall cannot continue to approve the demolition of rental housing for the construction of condos that are unaffordable for citizens.
cells.why: Commits to stopping rental-to-unaffordable-condo demolition, which is a comparable tenant-protection / demoviction instrument. Not the same as a demoviction bylaw, STR licensing, or an indoor-heat standard. Protection of lower-cost rentals inside the M6 composition sentence is not scored again.

cells.quote: My approach is to build the working system needed to change that: clear responsibility, coordinated action with provincial and regional partners, measurable results, and tracking whether improvements actually last.
cells.why: Commits to a coordinated homelessness-delivery system. Comparable to M11's Housing First + STEP operating system, not the same: Housing First and STEP are not named, no 50% unsheltered target, no quarterly count. Context, same section, not scored separately: "homelessness should be rare, brief and non-recurring, with no one left living on our streets"; "working together around individual transitions into permanent housing"; supportive and complex-care housing with treatment and recovery; "no discharge into homelessness from hospitals, corrections, detox, treatment or other public systems"; and challenging other governments when necessary to get housing built.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: We also need to start eliminating the hidden congestion tax paid by businesses, governments and individuals when people and goods sit unnecessarily in traffic.
cells.why: Commits to cutting congestion as a municipal cost. No adaptive-signal programme, no Vision Zero audit, no named corridor, no calming design. Context, same block, not scored separately: better transit and transportation planning to move more people while freeing road space for businesses, emergency services and people who need to drive.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target
culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
cells.quote: Victoria should be a place where artists, musicians, performers, writers, designers and cultural organizations can live, work and create.
cells.why: Agrees with an arts-ecosystem goal. No funding floor, no dollar, no sport. 2018 ProArt answers are not a 2026 source.

cells.quote: Treat every tax dollar, public asset and major project as a public trust: know what it costs, what it is supposed to achieve and whether people received value for their money.
cells.why: Agrees with the value-for-money test M65 exists to serve. No zero-based cycle, no grant threshold, no three-part test, no savings number.

cells.quote: Set clear goals, assign responsibility, measure results, finish what works and fix what doesn’t.
cells.why: Commits to a goals-responsibility-results operating method. No dashboard, no KPI set, no quarterly cadence. Context, not scored separately: "City Hall should know whether an initiative actually solved the problem or merely moved it somewhere else," and major-decision public accounting (what was spent, why, who benefited, what the public received, where revenue was forgone).

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging

cells.quote: Victoria needs practical action on building efficiency, extreme heat and wildfire smoke, resilient public facilities, water management, local food security, public transit and active transportation.
cells.why: Agrees with operational climate action and names comparable instruments (building efficiency, heat/smoke, resilient facilities). Not the same as M58's 50%/2030 set, district energy, or a seismic programme. Transit and active transportation in this sentence are not given a second mark on row 27 or 49.

cells.what: trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness

cells.quote: Engagement should happen early enough for people to genuinely influence decisions, not after the important choices have already been made.
cells.why: Commits to consultation before commitment, with no 25-million referendum threshold, no 5-step sequence and no material-change rule.

cells.quote: Good decisions start by listening to residents, frontline workers, businesses, community organizations and people with direct experience, then showing how what we heard affected the decision.
cells.why: Commits to a published account of how input changed the decision, which is comparable to M79b's 60-day consultation-response standard. Not the same office (no Integrity Commissioner, no MNP tracker, no 60-day clock). Context, not scored separately: "Residents should know what is actually open for decision, see a fair account of what was heard, and understand how their input affected the result."

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
